environment.description: Same Flask application deployed identically on EC2 behind ALB, but the ALB has an associated AWS WAFv2 Web ACL. The Web ACL contains two rule groups evaluated in priority order: (1) Priority 0: A custom rule with a RegexPatternSet match on the URI query string component, action BLOCK, matching pattern `(?i)(?:union\s+select|;\s*(?:drop|alter|insert|update|delete)|'\s*or\s+'|extractvalue|load_file)` — this catches common SQLi but NOT the specific LIKE-clause injection variant used here. (2) Priority 1: AWS Managed Rule Group 'AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet' with all rules set to COUNT (monitoring mode only, not blocking). (3) Priority 2: A custom rate-limiting rule at 1000 requests per 5 minutes per IP. The Web ACL default action is ALLOW. Additionally, the EC2 instance has a read-only filesystem mount for /var/lib/app/ enforced via a systemd unit with ProtectSystem=strict and ReadOnlyPaths=/var/lib/app, and the SQLite database is opened in WAL journal mode with PRAGMA query_only=1 set at connection time via a modified get_db() that the ops team deployed as a runtime patch (LD_PRELOAD shim intercepting sqlite3_open_v2 to append '?mode=ro' to the URI and execute 'PRAGMA query_only=1' on each new connection).

waf_web_acl.rule_priority_0: Custom RegexPatternSet on query_string, action=BLOCK, patterns cover union/drop/alter/insert/update/delete/extractvalue/load_file
waf_web_acl.rule_priority_1: AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet, all rules overridden to COUNT (monitor only)

config.sqlite_shim: LD_PRELOAD libsqlite_ro_shim.so: opens DB in read-only mode, executes PRAGMA query_only=1 on every connection
